__1 An evil spirit, a demon; the chief of the evil spirits; वृकद्वरसो असुरस्य वीरान् [[

.]] the [[Rām.]] thus accounts for the name:- सुराप्रतिग्रहाद्देवाः सुरा इत्यभिविश्रुताः । अप्रतिग्रहणात्तस्या दैतेयाश्चासुरास्तथा ॥ In the oldest parts of the Ṛgveda the term Asura is used for the Supreme Spirit and in the sense of 'god', 'divine'; it was applied to several of the chief deities such as Indra, Agni, and especially Varuṇa. It afterwards acquired an entirely opposite meaning, and came to signify a demon or an enemy of the gods. The Brāhmaṇas state that Prajāpati created Asuras with the breath (Asu); particularly from the lower breath. The [[Vāyu P.]] says that Asuras were first produced as sons from Prajāpati's groin; cf. also [[Nir.]] above].
